items.description: Saudi-backed forces say they are moving troops from the Bab al-Mandab Strait to defend the interim capital Aden.
items.imageCaption: Image caption, Pro-government forces said troops were being moved to defend the interim capital, Aden (file photo) | Figure caption, Watch: Why is the Bab al-Mandab Strait so important?
items.author: Katy Watson
items.excerpt: Yemeni pro-government forces backed by Saudi Arabia have said they are withdrawing from an area overlooking the strategically important Bab al-Mandab Strait, leaving it under the control of the Iran-backed Houthi movement. Yemen's military said it was redeploying troops from the key shipping gateway at the southern end of the Red Sea to defend its interim capital, Aden. The shift ends a weeks-long offensive to try to secure the area near the waterway after the Houthis seized it in a surprise offensive in September, squeezing global oil exports and prompting thousands to flee.
